title: The Shadow in the Cedars
lyrics:
Act II: The Shadow in the Cedars (The Guardian / Sasquatch)
(Tempo shifts to 85 BPM — Deep, resonating cedar flutes, ambient forest sounds, low thumping bass)

(Spoken Transition)

The Guardian:

"Bondzee. You listen to the two-legged ones who fly across the sky.

Now listen to the one who walks beneath the roots.

Before the canoes came, before the iron rails split the mountains, I was here.

They call me a monster. A shadow. A secret to be hunted.

I send you this song from the mist of the Fraser Valley."

(Verse 2 — The Guardian)

Dear Bondzee, the fog rolls heavy tonight on the mountain

The moss on the Douglas fir hangs thick as wool

I drink from the glacier, the ancient rock fountain

In a silence so heavy, the valley is full

I watched when the first fires were lit by the river

I watched when the Sts'ailes sang songs to the bear

I am the heartbeat that makes the leaves shiver

The breath in the fog that dissolves in the air.

(Pre-Chorus — The Guardian)

Now they come with their cameras, their steel, and their shouting

Searching for footprints I leave in the clay

They want to capture a god just to finish their doubting

So I step in the shadow and vanish away—

Do they know what I’ve seen?

Five thousand years of the gray and the green.

(Chorus — The Guardian)

Oh, Bondzee, my song-pal, write back through the timber

Tell me the mountains still belong to the wild

My stride is still long and my spirit is limber

Though the earth that I walk is no longer a child

I hide in the mist where the cedar trees weep

While the rest of the country is falling asleep

You’re the only one listening, the only one true

So I’m singing the song of the forest to you.
